subject.title: feat: wire live transcript and sync API contract

question: What permission and deployment boundary should ClickClack require before core can expose local Claude Code transcript files through an HTTP API?
rationale: The PR crosses auth, local-machine transcript privacy, and deployment-default boundaries; automation can point to the unsafe paths but cannot choose the product/security model for host-local transcript access.

options.title: Require a local/admin transcript boundary
options.body: Restore loopback-only token minting, keep normal installs off by default, and expose transcripts only behind an explicit maintainer-approved local/admin/debug permission model.

options.title: Sponsor a constrained deployment feature
options.body: Accept the feature direction only with documented operator constraints, a dedicated transcript permission, and explicit dev-auth expectations.

options.title: Move the bridge out of core
options.body: If this is specific to one host or workflow, pause this PR and implement the bridge as private deployment code or a plugin-oriented integration instead.

recommendation.title: Require a local/admin transcript boundary
recommendation.body: Restore loopback-only token minting, keep normal installs off by default, and expose transcripts only behind an explicit maintainer-approved local/admin/debug permission model.

likelyOwner.reason: The current auth boundary, same-origin helper, server routing baseline, and dev proxy baseline trace to Peter Steinberger's commit history in the affected files.
